13569.heading: Dream Text Ultrametricity
13569.content:
The book maps collections of dream reports and their words into a full Euclidean correspondence-analysis factor space, then counts approximately ultrametric triangles among text-unit locations. In its case studies, dream reports show a higher measured tendency than several literary and technical text collections.

The coefficient is sensitive to corpus selection, text segmentation, word encoding, dimensionality, and the angular rule used to count triangles. It characterizes relationships in written reports after conscious narration; it is not a direct measurement of the dreamer's unconscious neural activity.

13575.title: Dramatic Action
13575.heading: Dramatic Action
13575.content:
A dramatic action is a player action that changes the direction of the plot and therefore the story events the player can experience later. It is more specific than an action that merely overcomes a gameplay challenge.

The game must communicate the action's consequences well enough for agency to be meaningful. A choice that changes only hidden data or reconverges immediately without perceptible effect may feel dramatic in code but not in experience.

This monotonic relationship supports efficient pruning: failed candidates eliminate entire branches of the combinatorial search.

13584.title: Downward Causality
13584.heading: Downward Causality
13584.content:
Downward causality is the influence of an emergent whole on the parts that produce it. Once a higher-level pattern exists, it changes the environment, constraints, or opportunities within which lower-level parts act.

Together with [[Upward Causality]], it makes causation in a [[System Hierarchy]] reciprocal across levels. A game system can emerge from many local actions while its resulting state then reshapes each player's next decision.

13590.heading: Double-Slit Interference
13590.content: Double-slit interference occurs when coherent waves from two narrow openings overlap. Bright or strong maxima occur where path difference is an integer multiple of wavelength; minima occur at half-integer multiples. For slit separation $d$, maxima satisfy $d\sin\theta=m\lambda$. The pattern demonstrates the wave behavior of light and matter.

13593.title: Double Quantization Artifact
13593.heading: Double Quantization Artifact
13593.content:
A double quantization artifact is the periodic over- and under-population of transform-coefficient values produced by rounding at one step size and then at another. Some values from the first quantizer map disproportionately into the bins of the second, leaving a comb-like statistical pattern.

The pattern is evidence of two incompatible JPEG quantization histories and can sometimes be localized to edited regions. Its visibility depends on coefficient frequency, image content, alignment, and the relationship between the two tables.

13596.sourceSearchName: double angle identities double angle identities
13596.title: Double-Angle Identities
13596.heading: Double-Angle Identities
13596.content:
Setting the two angles equal in the [[Angle Addition Identities]] gives

$$\sin 2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$$

and

$$\cos2\theta=\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta.$$

The [[Pythagorean Trigonometric Identity]] rewrites the cosine formula as $2\cos^2\theta-1$ or $1-2\sin^2\theta$.

13605.sourceSearchName: double jpeg compression double jpeg compression
13605.title: Double JPEG Compression
13605.heading: Double JPEG Compression
13605.content:
Double JPEG compression occurs when a JPEG image is decoded and encoded again. The first save constrains transform coefficients to multiples determined by its quantization table; the second rounding acts on that already quantized distribution.

When the two quantization steps differ, their interaction can create periodic gaps or peaks in coefficient histograms. If the steps are identical, the second save may leave little distinguishable evidence, so absence of a double-compression trace does not exclude prior processing.

13608.title: Doppler Ultrasound
13608.heading: Doppler Ultrasound
13608.content: Doppler ultrasound measures blood-flow velocity from the frequency shift of sound reflected by moving blood cells. The shift depends on transmitted frequency, flow speed, sound speed, and the angle between beam and motion. Incorrect angle estimation can strongly bias the calculated speed, especially as the beam approaches perpendicular incidence.

13611.title: Double Buffering
13611.heading: Double Buffering
13611.content:
Double buffering renders the next image into a back buffer while the display presents a completed front buffer. When drawing finishes, the buffers exchange roles so the viewer receives a whole frame instead of watching individual drawing operations.

The technique reduces visible flicker and supports synchronization with the [[Vertical Blank Interval]]. It does not by itself prevent [[Screen Tearing]] if the swap occurs while the display is scanning the image.

13614.title: dotnet CLI
13614.heading: dotnet CLI
13614.content:
The `dotnet` command-line interface creates projects, restores packages, builds source, runs applications, executes tests, and publishes deployment output. Its commands provide a common workflow across operating systems and editors.

Project templates establish the initial SDK and target framework configuration, while later commands operate from the project file's declared dependencies. Command help and template listings make the tool self-describing enough to discover available operations without an IDE-specific menu.

13617.title: Dot Product
13617.heading: Dot Product
13617.content:
For planar vectors $u=(u_1,u_2)$ and $v=(v_1,v_2)$, the dot product is $u\cdot v=u_1v_1+u_2v_2$. The result is a scalar. It also satisfies $u\cdot v=\|u\|\|v\|\cos\theta$, so a zero dot product identifies perpendicular nonzero vectors and the sign records whether their angle is acute or obtuse.

With normalized vectors, a game can use the dot product directly as the cosine of the angle between directions. The sign quickly distinguishes whether a target is generally in front of, beside, or behind an object's facing direction.

13620.title: Doolittle Decomposition
13620.heading: Doolittle Decomposition
13620.content:
Doolittle decomposition is an [[LU Decomposition]] convention in which the diagonal entries of $L$ are all one. The remaining lower-triangular entries and the entries of $U$ are determined successively.

After factorization, [[Forward Substitution]] solves $Ly=b$ and [[Back Substitution]] solves $Ux=y$. Zero pivots may require row permutation.

13622.title: Doppler Satellite Position Fix

13623.sourceSearchName: doppler satellite position fix doppler satellite position fix
13623.title: Doppler Satellite Position Fix
13623.heading: Doppler Satellite Position Fix
13623.content: A Doppler satellite position fix compares the known transmitted frequency with the frequency received as a satellite approaches and recedes. If the satellite orbit is known, the shape and inflection of the frequency-shift curve constrain the receiver's location. Transit used this method for ships and submarines, but a useful fix required observing a pass and was difficult for fast-moving aircraft. GPS instead uses code travel time for rapid range measurements while still using Doppler-sensitive tracking for velocity and carrier acquisition.

13626.title: Doppler Effect
13626.heading: Doppler Effect
13626.content: The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency caused by relative motion between a wave source and observer. Approach compresses successive wavefronts and raises the received frequency; recession spreads them and lowers it. For sound the medium defines wave speed, while electromagnetic Doppler shifts require relativistic treatment at high relative speed.

13629.title: Domain Service
13629.heading: Domain Service
13629.content: A domain service expresses domain behavior that does not naturally belong to one entity or value object. Its interface is defined inside the domain model using the [[Ubiquitous Language]], while an implementation that calls a database or remote system can remain in the [[Application Layer]]. This direction keeps the model free of infrastructure dependencies. Domain services should not become a place to move all behavior out of entities; they are for genuine domain operations whose responsibility spans or sits outside individual objects.

13632.title: Donkey Space
13632.heading: Donkey Space
13632.content:
Donkey space is the tangle of recursive anticipation created when multiple players try to infer one another's plans while knowing that the others are doing the same. Each participant reasons about what the others know, expect, and may pretend to intend.

This layered mind-reading expands [[Yomi]] into a shared structure of uncertainty. It helps explain why competitive human play can generate forms of [[Multiplayer Complexity]] and surprise that fixed rules alone do not supply.

13634.sourceSearchName: don t repeat yourself principle don t repeat yourself principle
13634.title: Don't Repeat Yourself Principle
13634.heading: Document

13635.sourceSearchName: don t repeat yourself principle don t repeat yourself principle
13635.title: Don't Repeat Yourself Principle
13635.heading: Don't Repeat Yourself Principle
13635.content: Don't Repeat Yourself (DRY) asks that a single rule or behavior have one authoritative representation. Copying code into several classes makes a change require coordinated edits and creates opportunities for the copies to diverge. A shared abstraction can remove that burden when the copies express the same underlying requirement; superficially similar code should not be forced together if it changes for different reasons.

13638.title: Dominant Strategy
13638.heading: Dominant Strategy
13638.content:
A dominant strategy is so effective that a player has no meaningful reason to use an alternative. Its existence narrows the decision space and makes other mechanics strategically irrelevant.

Balance work should change costs, risks, counters, circumstances, or rewards so several strategies remain situationally useful. A strategy available to only one side can also make an asymmetric game unfair.

13641.title: Domain-Specific Computational Skill
13641.heading: Domain-Specific Computational Skill
13641.content:
Computational skill becomes powerful when joined to the concepts and practices of a domain. A learner may understand loops and data structures yet remain unable to formulate a meaningful model in physics, biology, or history.

Education should therefore connect computational methods to authentic disciplinary questions. Transfer is more plausible when teachers explicitly bridge representations, assumptions, and evidence between contexts.

13644.heading: Dominant Physics Selection for Thermal Problems
13644.content:
A model should include the mechanisms that materially affect its intended result. Conduction may dominate inside a solid, fluid motion may make convection essential, surface temperatures may make radiation significant, and phase change may add latent-energy behavior.

Adding every possible effect increases data requirements and numerical coupling without guaranteeing a better prediction. A defensible selection connects the [[Thermal Management Goals|question of interest]] to expected scales, available evidence, and a planned sensitivity check for effects initially treated as negligible.

13647.title: Dominant Eigenvalue
13647.heading: Dominant Eigenvalue
13647.content:
A dominant eigenvalue has strictly greater absolute value than every other eigenvalue of a matrix. Repeated multiplication then makes its eigenvector component dominate a generic starting vector.

This behavior supports the [[Power Method]]. If the largest magnitudes are tied or the starting vector has no component in the dominant eigendirection, the expected convergence may fail.

13650.heading: Domain Object Factory
13650.content: A domain object factory is a named function or method that creates a valid [[Value Object]] or [[Domain Entity]]. It can validate input, convert an external representation, and choose a construction path while keeping an invalid intermediate object from escaping. Multiple factories can make different sources explicit, such as constructing a title from plain text or from sanitized HTML. The factory belongs with the domain type when the creation rules are part of the type's meaning.

13653.heading: Domain Name System
13653.content:
The Domain Name System maps human-readable domain names to network addresses used by hosts and routers. It lets an application identify a service by a stable name while the corresponding address can be maintained separately.

DNS resolution is a distributed lookup rather than a property inherent in the name. A network client must therefore account for lookup delay, unavailable resolvers, and names that resolve to several addresses.

13656.title: Domain Model
13656.heading: Domain Model
13656.content: A domain model is a representation in the [[Solution Space]] that expresses domain concepts, state, and behavior in a form software can enforce. It should use the [[Ubiquitous Language]] and make rules discoverable in the model rather than scattering them through controllers or database procedures. A model is selective: it includes what is needed to solve the chosen problem, not every fact about the real world. Unlike an [[Anemic Domain Model]], it incorporates the operations that change its state.

The model remains focused on business behavior and can be tested without a database, web server, or mocking of technical services. Interfaces for required [[Domain Service]]s may live inside the model while their implementations live outside it. 13662.title: Domain Knowledge
13662.heading: Domain Knowledge
13662.content: Domain knowledge is understanding of the field in which software will operate, including its terminology, constraints, processes, and goals. It lets developers speak productively with experts rather than relying only on a requirements document. No single expert necessarily possesses the whole truth, so knowledge should be collected from people at different levels and in adjacent areas. This collaborative learning process is [[Knowledge Crunching]] and supplies the material for a [[Ubiquitous Language]].

13665.heading: Domain Dependence of Advanced Computational Thinking
13665.content:
Advanced computational thinking depends on the application domain. Programming skill alone does not supply the fluid dynamics needed for aircraft simulation, the biology needed for genome analysis, or the institutional knowledge needed for hospital software.

Productive collaboration therefore requires learning enough of the domain to recognize meaningful variables, constraints, and evidence. Computational methods add power to domain expertise; they do not replace it.

13668.title: Domain Event
13668.heading: Domain Event
13668.content: A domain event is a fact that changed the state of the domain. It describes something that happened, not something an actor wanted to do, so EventStorming names it with a subject and a past-tense verb such as “Order Confirmed.” Events are placed on an [[Event Timeline]] to reveal causal and temporal relationships. In implementation, the same fact can become an object raised by a [[Domain Entity]] or [[Aggregate]] and later stored through [[Event Sourcing]].

13671.title: Domain Entity
13671.heading: Domain Entity
13671.content: A domain entity represents a unique object whose identity persists while its attributes and state change. Two entities with identical current property values can still be different because they have different [[Entity Identity]] values. The entity exposes behavior in the [[Ubiquitous Language]] and protects transitions with [[Entity Invariant]]s. This meaning is distinct from a generic database row or a named entity extracted from language: its defining concern is continuity of identity through a life cycle.

13674.title: Document Similarity Clustering
13674.heading: Document Similarity Clustering
13674.content:
Document similarity clustering groups texts from a representation of their lexical or semantic proximity. Choices include term vectors, latent factors, graph links, language-model scores, and combinations of content with metadata.

The similarity definition determines whether clusters reflect topic, style, source, or another property. Evaluation should therefore inspect representative terms and documents rather than relying only on an internal geometric score.

Consistent ordering and a readable legend are essential for tracing each subgroup across the chart.

13680.sourceSearchName: domain and range domain and range
13680.title: Domain and Range
13680.heading: Domain and Range
13680.content: The domain of a [[Function]] is the set of permitted inputs, while its range is the set of outputs the function actually attains. A formula can impose restrictions: denominators cannot be zero and an even root of a real expression requires a nonnegative radicand. The range is determined by both the rule and the chosen domain.

13681.sourceSearchName: domain and range domain and range
13681.title: Domain and Range
13681.heading: References

13683.title: Document Database
13683.heading: Document Database
13683.content:
A document database stores records as self-describing documents rather than rows constrained to one relational table shape. Documents can contain the fields needed for an application object and are commonly addressed through a collection and a unique identifier.

The book presents Cosmos DB as the successor branding for Microsoft's DocumentDB service and accesses work-item documents through a MongoDB-compatible API. Document flexibility does not remove the need for deliberate identifiers, query patterns, and capacity planning.

13686.title: Dockerfile
13686.heading: Dockerfile
13686.content:
A Dockerfile is the declarative build recipe for a Docker image. Its instructions choose base images, copy and build application content, establish the runtime entry point, and can use multiple stages to keep the final artifact focused.

Visual Studio generates the book's initial Dockerfile when Linux container support is added. The file remains the reproducible source for rebuilding the image rather than relying on the state of one developer machine.

13689.title: Docker Image
13689.heading: Docker Image
13689.content:
A Docker image is the packaged, versionable template used to start one or more containers. It contains the application layers and dependencies described by its Dockerfile but does not become a running process until a container is created from it.

The sales-order image is built locally, tested with `docker run`, tagged, and uploaded to a registry. Kubernetes then refers to that registered image when creating its worker pods.

13692.title: Docker Container
13692.heading: Docker Container
13692.content:
A Docker container is an isolated running instance created from an image that packages an application and its dependencies. It avoids relying on a target machine to reproduce the exact library and framework environment used during development and testing.

The book runs its .NET Core 3 worker in a Linux container. The container is lighter than copying an entire virtual machine because it packages the application environment while remaining abstracted from much of the host operating system.

13695.title: DNA Computing
13695.heading: DNA Computing
13695.content:
DNA computing represents candidate solutions with molecular strands and uses biochemical operations to transform and select them. Early demonstrations encoded paths through a graph and evolved a mixture toward strands representing valid or short routes.

Its operations are massively parallel but governed by chemistry rather than a CPU instruction cycle. Effective design therefore requires molecular biology as well as computational abstraction.

13698.title: Divisive Clustering
13698.heading: Divisive Clustering
13698.content:
Divisive clustering begins with the complete data set in one cluster and repeatedly splits groups until every observation is separate or another stopping condition is reached.

A divisive method must choose both which cluster to divide and how to divide it. Binary-feature methods and full-variable methods impose different structural assumptions on that choice.

13700.title: Divisibility

13701.title: Divisibility
13701.heading: Divisibility
13701.content:
An integer a divides b when b = ak for some integer k. Divisibility organizes multiples and factors without requiring a numerical quotient operation inside every algebraic setting.

It supports definitions of greatest common divisors, relatively prime integers, and modular arithmetic.

13704.heading: Divide and Conquer
13704.content:
Divide and conquer solves a problem by breaking it into smaller instances, solving those instances, and combining their results. The decomposition repeats until each subproblem is simple enough to solve directly.

Repeated halving explains why logarithms frequently appear in algorithm analysis. [[Binary Search]] keeps only one half of its search space, while [[Merge Sort]] solves both halves and combines their ordered results with a [[Merge Operation]].

13707.title: Divided Difference
13707.heading: Divided Difference
13707.content:
A divided difference is a recursively defined coefficient based on function values at distinct nodes. The first divided difference is $f[x_i,x_{i+1}]=(f(x_{i+1})-f(x_i))/(x_{i+1}-x_i)$.

Higher orders compare lower-order divided differences over wider node intervals. A divided-difference table supplies the coefficients for [[Newton Divided Difference Interpolation]].

13716.title: Distributive Property
13716.heading: Distributive Property
13716.content:
The distributive property connects multiplication with addition:

$$a(b+c)=ab+ac,$$

and similarly ((a+b)c=ac+bc). A factor outside parentheses multiplies every term inside them.

Distribution is the basis of [[Polynomial Expansion]] and [[Combining Like Terms]]. Used in reverse, it becomes [[Polynomial Factorization]] because a repeated factor can be taken outside a sum. The rule does not imply that every operation distributes over addition; for example, ((a+b)^2) is generally not (a^2+b^2) because expansion also produces the cross term (2ab).

13719.title: Distributional Equivalence
13719.heading: Distributional Equivalence
13719.content:
Two rows or columns are distributionally equivalent when their normalized profiles are identical. In correspondence analysis, identical profiles occupy the same position and have zero profile distance. Adding their counts together preserves their profile and therefore does not alter the mutual distances that depend on that profile.

This permits exact-profile aggregation before an expensive analysis and can make a display easier to interpret. Near-equivalent profiles require an approximation judgment: combining them changes the data slightly, so the accepted loss should be checked against the study's resolution.

13722.title: Distributional Effects of AI
13722.heading: Distributional Effects of AI
13722.content:
The distributional effects of AI are the ways a system's benefits, burdens, errors, and risks are allocated across people and groups. A system can improve average efficiency while concentrating surveillance, unemployment, unsafe conditions, or false accusations among those with less power.

Ethical evaluation therefore asks "improvement for whom?" rather than relying only on total performance. Stakeholders include people who never chose to use the system but are classified or affected by it. Distributional analysis connects technical measures to [[AI and Economic Inequality]] and reveals when a claimed social benefit depends on transferring costs to a vulnerable population.

Distribution-based feature utility estimates the value of a transformation from how it changes feature or class distributions, without fully training a downstream model. Divergence and separability measures can provide inexpensive search guidance.

The proxy accelerates exploration but may not align perfectly with eventual predictive performance. It is most useful when its assumptions match the task and expensive candidates receive later model-based confirmation.

13728.title: Distribution Sampling
13728.heading: Distribution Sampling
13728.content:
Distribution sampling generates values whose frequencies approximate a probability distribution. Samples allow expectations, probabilities, and other summaries to be estimated even when direct integration is difficult.

A valid sampling method must account for any difference between the distribution used to generate candidates and the target distribution. Accuracy improves with effective independent sample count, not merely raw iterations.

13731.heading: Distributed Transaction Limitation
13731.content:
A distributed transaction limitation appears when one business operation changes state owned by separate services or databases that cannot participate in one ordinary local transaction. At a particular instant, one part may have committed while another has not.

The order-processing discussion contrasts this with a single database transaction that can update an order and stock together. Distributed designs need asynchronous coordination and explicit recovery or compensation rather than assuming every component changes atomically.

13734.title: Distributed System
13734.heading: Distributed System
13734.content:
A distributed system divides work among independently executing processes that communicate across boundaries rather than sharing one in-process state. This can support independent scaling and deployment, but failures and timing become partial: one component may succeed while another is unavailable.

The book's sales-order system separates message production, queued transport, order persistence, and confirmation. Its design gains resilience to traffic spikes while accepting more complex data integrity, logging, maintenance, and user-experience decisions.

13737.title: Distributed Software Transactional Memory
13737.heading: Distributed Software Transactional Memory
13737.content:
Distributed software transactional memory coordinates reads and writes to shared objects as optimistic transactions spanning multiple machines. An operation records its accesses, then commits atomically if concurrent work has not invalidated them.

The model can reduce explicit lock management and its deadlock, livelock, convoying, and composability problems. Conflicts can still waste work, which motivates a [[Transactional Scheduler]].

13740.heading: Distributed Scene Graph
13740.content:
A distributed scene graph shares a spatial object hierarchy across multiple processes or computers. Participants can render individual viewpoints or operate separate devices while referring to consistent object identities and transformations.

Updates must be communicated and ordered without assuming zero network delay. The design may replicate selected graph state near each renderer while defining which component owns authoritative changes.

13743.heading: Distributed Object System
13743.content:
A distributed object system lets software objects communicate across process or host boundaries through an interface that resembles local interaction. In AR, tracking, simulation, rendering, and device services may run on different computers while participating in one application.

Distribution can place work near specialized hardware and share state among users. Network delay, partial failure, serialization, and object identity remain real concerns even when the programming abstraction hides connection details.

13746.title: Distributed Logging
13746.heading: Distributed Logging
13746.content:
Distributed logging collects diagnostic events from multiple services and short-lived containers into a form that can be searched as one system history. Writing only to a container's local file is unreliable because that filesystem may disappear with the instance.

The order-processing chapter suggests a managed service such as Application Insights or a logging queue with a dedicated consumer. Entries need enough service and execution context to separate simultaneous writers and reconstruct a cross-service operation.

13749.heading: Distributed IT Function
13749.content:
A distributed IT function embeds technology capability in business units rather than concentrating every operational decision in one central department. Local teams can select and use cloud services close to the needs they support.

A shared leadership role still defines standards, governance, and audit expectations, while finance and procurement can manage billing and contracts. Distribution improves responsiveness only when the organization preserves common security, integration, and service-management practices.

Distributed feature selection divides feature-scoring or subset-search work across multiple processors or machines. It addresses datasets whose number of records, variables, or pairwise relationships exceed one machine's practical resources.

Distribution introduces communication and coordination costs, so a method should minimize repeated movement of the data. The selected result must also remain stable and interpretable across partitions.

13758.content:
Distributed development places whole teams at different locations, while a dispersed team separates members of the same team across locations. Both add communication delay, but dispersed membership disrupts the dense daily collaboration inside a team more directly.

Keeping teams locally cohesive where possible, overlapping working hours, making work visible, and investing in rich communication reduce—but do not eliminate—the distance cost.

Distance-based level of detail uses a detailed asset near the camera and progressively simpler representations farther away. Screen-space size, rather than world-space size alone, determines how much geometric or texture detail the player can actually perceive.

Well-chosen transitions reduce rendering cost without an obvious visual jump. Geometry levels work with [[Mipmap Chains for Distant Assets|texture mipmaps]] so both mesh and image sampling become cheaper as the asset occupies fewer pixels.

13773.title: Distance Preservation
13773.heading: Distance Preservation
13773.content:
Distance preservation measures how well a reduced representation retains the pairwise distances present in the original data. If most variation lies along a small number of directions, projecting onto those directions can approximate the original geometry with far fewer coordinates.

Preservation is approximate whenever discarded dimensions contain nonzero variation. Residual reconstruction error and comparisons of original with reduced distances reveal what the simplification loses.

13776.content:
The Strategy pattern packages a distance calculation as an interchangeable object. A clustering algorithm receives a Distance base pointer and calls its function operator without knowing whether the concrete measure is Euclidean, matching, mixed, or Mahalanobis.

Separating proximity from cluster control flow lets one algorithm be tested under several domain models. An algorithm that mathematically requires a particular distance should validate or construct that requirement instead of pretending every strategy is compatible.

13782.title: Distance Matrix
13782.heading: Distance Matrix
13782.content:
A distance matrix records the pairwise distance between every pair of observations. It is symmetric when the distance is symmetric, has zeros on its diagonal, and provides the input for many clustering and multidimensional-scaling procedures.

The source constructs one from high-dimensional gene-expression samples. The matrix preserves pairwise relationships without retaining the original feature coordinates, so its meaning depends entirely on the selected distance and preprocessing.

13785.title: Distance Concentration in High Dimensions
13785.heading: Distance Concentration in High Dimensions
13785.content:
Distance concentration occurs when nearest and farthest pairwise distances become increasingly similar as dimensionality grows under common data models. Irrelevant coordinates accumulate variation until proximity has little contrast.

The effect weakens the neighborhood assumptions used by many clusterers. Feature selection, subspace methods, alternative similarity functions, and domain-aware normalization attempt to recover informative contrast rather than trusting raw full-space distance.

Murtagh emphasizes another consequence in some sparse, high-dimensional settings: approximate equality of large distances can make many triples look equilateral or nearly ultrametric. This symmetry can support coarse hierarchical indexing, but it also makes the chosen representation and proximity test crucial. Data piling is a model- and distribution-dependent opportunity, not a blanket cure for weak distance contrast.

13788.title: Distance Between Points
13788.heading: Distance Between Points
13788.content:
The distance between $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ is

$$\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}.$$

The formula applies the [[Pythagorean Theorem]] to the horizontal and vertical coordinate differences. It is also the magnitude of the displacement vector joining the two points.

13791.title: Distance Attenuation
13791.heading: Distance Attenuation
13791.content:
Distance attenuation reduces the level of a spatial sound as the [[3D Sound Emitter]] moves farther from the [[3D Sound Listener]]. The falloff curve defines how quickly the sound changes between its near and far ranges.

The chosen curve is often tuned for gameplay clarity rather than strict physical realism. Important cues may remain audible farther away, while ambient sounds can fade more aggressively.

13794.title: Display Fidelity
13794.heading: Display Fidelity
13794.content:
Display fidelity is the degree to which sensory stimuli produced by a display correspond to those that would be present in the physical world.

It is not one score. Visual components include [[Field of View]], [[Field of Regard]], stereoscopic quality, [[Refresh Rate]], [[Spatial Resolution]], color quality, and [[Latency]]. Auditory fidelity includes sound quality, spatiality, and delay, while haptic fidelity includes resolution, delay, and the quality of force or touch.

One display has strictly higher fidelity than another only when all relevant components are at least as strong. More often, displays trade one component for another, so the task determines which profile is preferable.

13797.title: Display Space
13797.heading: Display Space
13797.content:
Display space is the set of physical and virtual surfaces through which an AR system can present information. It may include head-worn imagery, handheld screens, wall displays, projectors, and other devices distributed throughout the environment.

Unlike a single desktop window, this space can surround the user and change with location. Architecture must decide which content belongs on which display while preserving shared coordinates, continuity, privacy, and device capability.

13800.title: Displacement
13800.heading: Displacement
13800.content: Displacement is the vector change in position from an initial point to a final point. It records both magnitude and direction and therefore differs from distance traveled, which is a scalar path length. The gradient of a displacement-time graph is [[Linear Velocity]], while the area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement change.

13803.heading: Disjunctive Normal Form
13803.content:
A proposition is in disjunctive normal form when it is an OR of AND clauses whose terms are variables or negated variables. Each true row of a [[Truth Table]] supplies one conjunction: use the variable when the row assigns true and its negation when the row assigns false.

Taking the disjunction of these row clauses produces a formula with exactly the table's output behavior. This construction shows that AND, OR, and NOT gates can implement any Boolean input-output table used by a [[Electronic Circuits|combinatorial logic circuit]].

13824.heading: Discovering Blender Python Operators
13824.content:
Blender makes operator discovery an empirical process. A developer can perform the desired interface action, inspect the resulting call in the [[Blender Command Log]], and use Python tooltips or console autocompletion to inspect the operator's parameters.

The discovered call should then be tested in the current mode and selection state because many operators depend on `bpy.context`. This method turns ordinary interface use into API exploration while also revealing which actions map cleanly to `bpy.ops` and which require direct work with Blender data.
